We'd be happy to run a Dedicated-capacity demo and sizing session. A couple quick Qs so we can make the session productive:
- Is the 150ms p95 target for end-to-end user-facing latency or just model response time?
- Typical request size (tokens in / tokens out) and expected average RPS/concurrent users?
- Any strict compliance/network constraints (VPC, on-prem connectors)?

I looped in Aditya (SE) to run the technical deep-dive. Can you confirm availability for a 45-minute demo this week? A few slots I have open:

Or if none of those work, feel free to pick a time on my calendar: https://calendly.com/redwood/marissa-dedicated-demo.

Thanks — talk soon.

Answers: the 150ms p95 is an end-to-end target (including network). Typical payloads are ~80 tokens in / ~120 tokens out. We expect sustained periods of ~200 qps with peaks up to 800 qps during high-demand windows. We can provide a small sample traffic dump and a short architecture doc (will add Tom on the thread). No special compliance requirements beyond standard SOC2; VPC would be preferred.

Tom Sato (tom.sato@acme-logistics.com) — our infra lead — will join the call for the technical bits.

Thanks for the context — quick SE note before the demo:
- For p95 < 150ms end-to-end we'll want to separate network tail latency from model p95; in practice we design for model p95 ~ 50–80ms and allow 40–80ms for network + frontend.
- With your peak 800 qps and 200 qps sustained, recommended starting point is a 4-GPU dedicated pool (A100/H100 class depending on model) with autoscale headroom and a warm KV cache. We'll walk through exact numbers during the demo.
- Please share ~100 anonymized sample requests and an example concurrency trace if possible. Sample script I use attached.

Attaching: throughput-checklist.txt

I'll prepare a small JMeter-style workload to simulate 200 qps and a stress run for the peaked window in the demo.

—Aditya
SE, Redwood Inference
